title: Dev-to-Test Readiness Bridge and Final Dev Exhaustion Summary
authorityBoundary: Lowest-authority summary. Re-derived from the validator-enforced child maps and the current-main capability-service realisation map at HEAD. Defines no semantics; the verdict is evidence-backed by the referenced validator-enforced artefacts and does not self-assert authority.

nonRealisedItems.reason: A background worker/job runner needs a runtime worker substrate plus execution/failure negative-path proofs; realisation is a test-proof-ladder rung.
Runtime secrets management (write-only, redaction, no-read-back) is provable at the test rung with a local store; a live secret provider is a later rung.
Marked not-applicable-final and excluded from V2 scope (only a healthz route recorded); a later semantic decision is required before dev realisation.
Branding/theming is UI-facing configuration; the config CRUD is provable at the test rung but full realisation requires a UI, so it stays at the test-proof rung.
DNS ownership verification and TLS issuance require live DNS/ACME providers; realisation is live-provider, only canonical-set semantics are locally expressible.
Canonical-domain set/unset is a tenant config operation provable at the test rung (idempotent set/unset, fail-closed conflicts); no owning dev-now child.
Activating a tenant domain for an auth client requires a live identity-provider/auth-client integration; realisation is live-provider.
Write-only secret settings (no read-back, redaction) is provable at the test rung with negative-path proofs; a live secret provider is a later rung.
Catalog/lineage/PII-classification and DSR/GDPR flows require substantial substrate work with negative-path proofs; realisation sits at the test-proof rung.
A read-only history projection needs the event substrate plus a projection-consistency proof; realisation is a test-proof-ladder rung.
PITR, retention, legal hold and data residency depend on real storage-provider capabilities and deployment regions; not realisable with local dev routes.

Foundational storage with migrations and RLS needs an L4 substrate plus RLS negative-path and migration-rehearsal proofs; ownership spans migration and tenant-boundary concerns so it stays at the test rung.
Marked not-applicable-final and excluded from V2 scope; a later semantic decision is required before any dev realisation, so realisable only later.
OpenAPI route recorded but explicitly not claimed as a service realisation; it is a build/CI drift gate, deliberately semantic-only rather than a product capability.
Rate limiting requires runtime enforcement with a 429 negative-path proof on the substrate; realisation is a test-proof-ladder rung, not just a docs surface.
Webhook registration, signing and retry semantics need the event substrate plus a delivery/retry negative-path proof against mock endpoints on the test rung.
Product catalog/plans/prices CRUD is provable in dev/test but has no owning USF-1071..1077 child, so it stays at the test-proof rung pending a billing slice.
Quota enforcement needs a runtime counter plus an over-quota deny negative-path proof on the test rung.
Payment methods, invoices and dunning require a live payment provider (e.g. billing PSP) to realise; local routes cannot prove the semantic.
Meter-event ingestion and aggregation are provable in dev/test with substrate and idempotency proofs; realisation sits at the test-proof rung.
Durable queues with DLQ/redrive need an event substrate plus DLQ/redrive negative-path proofs on the test rung.
A workflow engine with approvals needs substrate plus workflow-state and approval negative-path proofs; realisation is a test-proof-ladder rung.
A decision-framework/principles capability describing how USF chooses build vs compose; it is a semantic policy, not a runtime service to realise.
Readyz local route recorded for completeness but explicitly not claimed as a client or service realisation; deliberately remains a semantic/support definition.
A methodology/principles capability defining the stage-aware confidence ladder itself; it is a semantic definition of the proof model, not a realisable runtime service.
Environment registry and bootstrap is inherently a deployment/staging concern (provisioning and wiring environments), so realisation requires a staged deployment rung, not local dev routes.
A modelling/principles capability describing the shared-vs-environment-specific service model; semantic policy, not a runtime service.
Runtime i18n and translation validation is provable via a dev/test rung (missing-key/validation checks) but has no owning USF-1071..1077 child, so it stays at the test-proof rung.
The USF scope-and-principles charter; a foundational semantic definition, not a runtime capability to realise.

API keys/PATs need real token issuance, hashing, scoping and revocation beyond a negative-path proof; the invalid/expired/revoked-key deny path is provable at the test rung, so realisation sits at the test-proof rung.
Delegated administration needs a role/scope model plus a deny-beyond-delegated-scope negative-path proof; realisation is a test-proof-ladder rung.
Self-service profile/preferences is UI-facing; CRUD is provable at the test rung but full realisation requires a UI, so it stays at the test-proof rung.
The entitlement engine needs a policy/model plus a not-entitled deny negative-path proof; realisation is a test-proof-ladder rung.
Sub-organisations need a hierarchy data model plus cross-sub-org isolation negative-path proofs; realisation is a test-proof-ladder rung.
Tenant groups need a grouping model plus membership/isolation proofs; realisation is a test-proof-ladder rung.
Contract explicitly deprecated and superseded by observability-built-in-alerting-and-incidents; retained as lineage only, not a current realisation claim.
Grafana Faro RUM and browser-to-BFF tracing require a live external telemetry provider/backend to realise; cannot be proven with local dev routes alone.
Log aggregation and tenant-scoped search require an external log-store/search backend provider to realise meaningfully.
Alerting/incident/on-call realisation needs a live metrics+notification/on-call provider chain; only rule semantics are local, full realisation is live-provider.
Product search/indexing requires an external search-engine provider to realise; local dev routes cannot prove the indexing/query semantic.
A code-quality/secret/dependency scanning gate is realised and proven at the CI/test rung; there is no runtime product surface.
Support tickets/customer-health/announcements is a UI-facing product feature; CRUD is provable at the test rung but full realisation needs a UI.
Tenant lifecycle (provision/suspend/delete/export) needs substrate state transitions plus fail-closed proofs; provisioning against real infra is a later rung, so it stays at the test rung.

verdictRationale: All bounded dev-realizable work is delivered and validator-enforced: the semantic sweep classifies all 67 semantic contracts; the 12 dev-realisable-now capabilities are each realised by an owning child deliverable (developer portal/docs, accessibility gate, operator workbench, provider consolidation, data rehearsal, auth negative-path catalogue, ISO 27001-aligned control map), each with a fail-closed validator and planted-defect selftest. All remaining work is explicitly classified into non-dev backlogs (test-rung, staging/deployment, live-provider, intentionally-semantic-only, deprecated) with rationale and next-rung. The move to test proof-ladder focus is deliberate, evidence-backed, and guarded by repository validators; it asserts no readiness.
